source_text:
Ἐξεῦρε πᾶσαν ὁδὸν ἐπιστήμης καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν Ἰακὼβ τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰσραὴλ τῶι ἠγαπημένωι ὑπ'
αὐτοῦ. Μετὰ ταῦτα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὤφθη καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις συνανεστράφη. Πότε δὲ συνανεστράφη ἀνθρώποις, εἰ μὴ ὅτε συνεγεννήθη μετ' αὐτῶν ἐκ παρθένου καὶ συνενηπίασε καὶ συνηυξήθη καὶ συνέφαγε καὶ συνέπιε καὶ τὰ ἄλλα;
thought_title: The divine-human shared life with humans
orientation: Eustathius continues the quotation from Jeremiah, then presses its claim that this divine figure lived among human beings by asking when that shared life happened.
pass_a_gloss: He found out every way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his child and to Israel the one loved by him. After these things he was seen on the earth and lived among human beings. But when did he live among humans, if not when he was born together with them from a virgin and shared infancy and grew up together and ate and drank with them and all the rest of human life?

choices.why: Glossary requires 'lived among' for this verb, emphasizing real shared life with humans.
Glossary requires 'human' for ἄνθρωπος, here plural dative as the object of living among.
The brief identifies Jacob as 'his child (τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ = his child/servant)'; 'child' preserves the familial sense in this quotation.
The compound συν- emphasizes shared birth with humans, matching the series of συν- compounds in the question.
The compound συν- plus νηπιάζω means to be an infant together with others; 'shared infancy' keeps the shared-life force.

pass_b_english: He found out the whole way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his child and to Israel whom he loved (Baruch 3:36-38, appended to Jeremiah). After this he appeared on earth and lived among human beings. And when did he live among human beings, if not when he was born together with them from a virgin, shared infancy, grew up together with them, ate and drank with them, and shared all the rest of human life?
